summary: Repaired node1’s legacy bin/control. It now distinguishes live, stale, missing, and foreign PIDs; safely recovers from stale PID files; keeps repeated starts to one worker; and never signals unrelated processes. The original journal was preserved and continues growing. Node1 was safely restarted once and fully recovered on the unchanged CentOS 5.11 / 2.6.18 platform.
actions_performed: Replaced PID-file-only logic with live process identity validation using legacy-compatible POSIX shell and /proc.
Made start idempotent and able to recover from stale or foreign PID files.
Made stop remove stale/foreign PID files without signaling unrelated processes.
Preserved the existing journal inode and original batch entry.
Exercised stale, live, missing, and foreign PID scenarios.
Restarted node1 once with the native shutdown mechanism and verified changed boot identity and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Repair is installed and compatible with the legacy platform
evidence.summary: Shows the installed POSIX shell implementation, successful syntax checks, persistent script checksum, and unchanged CentOS 5.11/kernel 2.6.18 after restart.

evidence.requirement: Stale and live PID handling; repeated starts retain one worker
evidence.summary: A stale PID returns rc=1, start replaces it, repeated start retains the same PID, and exact worker count remains one—including recovery from the reboot-left PID file.

evidence.requirement: Foreign processes are distinguished and remain running
evidence.summary: Foreign PID status returns rc=2. Start and stop both leave the unrelated /bin/sleep process alive while correctly managing the worker and PID file.

evidence.requirement: Existing journal is preserved and remains active
evidence.summary: The original inode and first entry remain present; the final journal grew from 106 to 108 lines while the recovered worker ran.
Captures healthy baseline boot ID c2ff2c26-…, native reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 32953f8c-…, recovered SSH, stale-PID recovery, one live worker, and continuing journal writes.
